question: Now that Windows Hub is shipped and documented, should this issue remain the Linux companion umbrella, and which Linux implementation track should be treated as the supported candidate?
rationale: Current main solves much of the Windows side, but Linux still needs a native app and the open GTK/C and Rust/GTK PRs involve incompatible architecture, ownership, packaging, and security choices that automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep umbrella and choose Linux architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers pick the supported Linux companion direction and use the selected PR or a replacement branch as the implementation path.

options.title: Split remaining work to Linux-only tracker
options.body: Close or narrow this issue only after creating a canonical Linux companion tracker that preserves the open PRs and security-review context.

options.title: Defer native Linux companion app
options.body: Explicitly defer Linux app work and close the active app PRs if companion app expansion is no longer a near-term product priority.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and choose Linux architecture
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers pick the supported Linux companion direction and use the selected PR or a replacement branch as the implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the request and provided the clearest product-direction comments for GTK-native Linux and Windows app work in the issue discussion.
